overview: Enprise Group is a small NZX-listed technology holding company whose dominant asset is Kilimanjaro Consulting, one of the largest MYOB Exo and MYOB Acumatica (formerly MYOB Advanced) implementation and support partners in Australia and New Zealand, servicing roughly 800 legacy MYOB Exo clients and around 350 MYOB Acumatica cloud ERP clients plus a majority-owned HubSpot marketing partner (Recipe Marketing, 52%). Enprise also wholly owns iSell (a small SaaS quoting tool for the managed-service-provider market) and holds minority equity-accounted/strategic stakes in Datagate Innovation (32.35%, telecom/utility billing SaaS) and Vadacom Holdings (6.4%, VoIP). The Group is a genuine micro-cap: FY2025 revenue was NZ$24.97m, operating profit only NZ$57k, net profit NZ$98k, and total equity just NZ$3.28m across ~20-21.8m shares on issue (post a small FY2026 rights issue).

business_model.summary: Enprise makes money almost entirely as a channel/implementation partner reselling and servicing third-party ERP and CRM software (MYOB Exo, MYOB Acumatica, HubSpot) rather than owning core IP for its main revenue lines. Revenue is a mix of one-off software/licence resale, implementation and consulting services (the largest line), hosting, and a smaller wholly-owned SaaS product (iSell/ITQuoter). Margins are thin because consulting/services revenue carries high, largely fixed employee-cost intensity, and because software/licence resale margins are set (and periodically contested) by the vendor, MYOB. The business is genuinely low margin-of-safety: FY2025 operating margin was ~0.2% of revenue and equity is a wafer-thin NZ$3.28m against NZ$25m of revenue and NZ$12m of liabilities.
business_model.customer_type: B2B, predominantly mid-market SMEs and mid-sized corporates in Australia and New Zealand using MYOB Exo (on-premise, legacy) or migrating to MYOB Acumatica (cloud); HubSpot CRM clients via Recipe Marketing
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2025: Australia ~71% of revenue (NZ$17.66m), New Zealand ~28% (NZ$7.10m), EMEA/North America negligible (~1%). Revenue is increasingly Australia-weighted.

main_competitors: Other MYOB Exo/Acumatica channel partners in ANZ
In-house IT/ERP teams at larger prospects
competitive_position.market_position: Kilimanjaro describes itself as the largest MYOB Exo installed base in Australia or New Zealand and one of the largest Acumatica (MYOB Acumatica) partners in the world; it has held MYOB Diamond/Platinum Partner status for roughly a decade and won MYOB Partner of the Year in 2023. This is a leadership position within a narrow, single-vendor ecosystem rather than broad ERP market share.

moat_factors.factor: Scale within the MYOB partner channel
moat_factors.description: Largest Exo installed base and a top-tier Acumatica partner gives referral flow, vendor co-marketing support, and negotiating weight versus smaller partners, but this scale exists entirely inside one vendor's ecosystem.

moat_factors.factor: Switching costs for existing ERP clients
moat_factors.description: Once a business has implemented Exo/Acumatica and built custom workflows/integrations, switching consultants (or systems) is costly and disruptive, supporting recurring support/hosting revenue and ~7%/yr on-premise attrition.

Support contracts and growing cloud (Acumatica) recurring revenue (recurring revenue reported up ~12% in 1H FY2026) provide some revenue visibility, though the business is still services-heavy and utilisation-dependent.
Repeated industry awards signal reputation, but brand equity does not transfer outside the MYOB/Acumatica/HubSpot partner ecosystems and provides no pricing power over the vendors themselves.

weaknesses: No proprietary core ERP technology for the dominant Kilimanjaro business — it resells and implements a vendor's product and is contractually and economically dependent on that vendor's terms.

Demonstrated vendor risk: MYOB attempted a unilateral ~43% margin cut in 2022 (worth ~NZ$935k/yr to Kilimanjaro) that required litigation and an Australian Federal Court injunction to resolve — the vendor relationship is not fully aligned with Kilimanjaro's interests.

MYOB Exo is a legacy, on-premise product; the FY2023-24 negotiated partner agreement guaranteed Kilimanjaro's rights to market Exo only 'until at least 31 December 2025' (Advanced/Acumatica for 5 years) — no independently verified public confirmation of a further Exo extension was found beyond management's 1H FY2026 commentary referencing an 'extended runway for Exo that MYOB has committed to.'
Thin capital base and history of large one-off losses (FY2023 goodwill/intangible impairment of NZ$7.7m against iSell/Kilimanjaro carrying values erased almost all equity that year).
Structural low margins: FY2025 operating margin ~0.2%, FY2026 H1 swung to an operating loss, meaning small revenue or cost shocks can flip the company from profit to loss.

growth_drivers: Migration of the ~800-strong MYOB Exo on-premise installed base to cloud MYOB Acumatica, which appears to carry a higher recurring-revenue/margin profile over time

Cross-sell/synergies between Kilimanjaro's ERP base and the majority-owned Recipe Marketing (HubSpot CRM) business, which has quickly become a HubSpot Diamond Partner and a top-10 HubSpot partner in the JAPAC region
AI features being embedded by both Acumatica and HubSpot, which management frames as a driver of client re-investment and technology spend
Improving SME business confidence/technology investment cycle in Australia and New Zealand after a soft FY2023-25 period

Continued growth at minority holdings Datagate Innovation (ARR growth, US market traction, successful oversubscribed capital raises) and Vadacom (EBITDA growth), which contribute equity-accounted gains/carrying-value uplift
Bolt-on M&A in adjacent software/services niches (Recipe Marketing acquired August 2024) — growth has clearly been augmented by acquisition, not purely organic

business.description: Kilimanjaro's core revenue depends on continued authorisation to sell and support MYOB Exo and MYOB Acumatica. MYOB has previously tried to unilaterally cut partner margins and compete more directly, and Exo's partner rights were only contractually secured to 31 December 2025 in the 2023 settlement; no independently confirmed public renewal beyond that date was located.

The business is a people-driven consultancy (~120+ Kilimanjaro staff) whose value is billable, skilled ERP consultants; utilisation, wage inflation, and staff retention directly drive the thin operating margin, and losing senior consultants or sales staff would be highly disruptive.

Long-serving Managing Director/CEO Ronnie Baskind (also Kilimanjaro CEO, described by the board as instrumental to the group's success over ~20 years) is departing 4 September 2026; Grant Harwood has been named interim CEO while a permanent search proceeds. Leadership transitions at a business this reliant on relationships (vendor, staff, clients) carry elevated execution risk.

MYOB Exo is an on-premise legacy product experiencing ~7%/yr client attrition as clients migrate to cloud alternatives; Kilimanjaro must successfully convert this base to Acumatica (or lose the revenue) while managing margin transition.

business.risk: Small, thin-margin base means limited buffer for execution mistakes
business.description: 1H FY2026 already swung from a NZ$0.12m operating profit to a NZ$0.62m operating loss on only modest (3.5%) revenue growth, driven by higher employee costs and utilisation — illustrating how quickly profitability can deteriorate.

financial.description: Total equity was only NZ$3.28m at 30 June 2025 (NZ$3.12m at 31 Dec 2025) against NZ$12-13m of liabilities; net tangible assets per share have been negative in several recent periods, leaving very little margin of safety for creditors or shareholders.

financial.risk: Recurring need for small capital raises
financial.description: The company completed a rights issue in the six months to 31 December 2025 (NZ$0.76m) plus a further NZ$0.12m shortfall placement in January 2026, evidencing an ongoing need to shore up the balance sheet/fund investment from a small capital base; this is dilutive to existing holders.

The majority of revenue (~71% in FY2025) is generated in Australia while the company reports in NZD, creating translation exposure on both the income statement and the AUD-denominated Kilimanjaro Australia balance sheet.

financial.risk: Bank debt secured over Group assets
financial.description: BNZ overdraft and term loan facilities are secured by a general security interest (PPSR) over the assets of Enprise, Kilimanjaro Consulting Pty and Kilimanjaro Consulting Ltd; while modest in absolute size (~NZ$1.1m at 31 Dec 2025), this represents a real claim ahead of equity in a low-equity company.

regulatory.description: The 2022-23 MYOB litigation specifically examined whether the Kilimanjaro/MYOB partnership agreement falls under Australian franchising codes; this indicates the legal characterisation and protections of the channel-partner relationship remain a live, only partially resolved question that could resurface.
As an FMC reporting entity on the NZX Main Board, Enprise bears governance, audit and disclosure costs that are proportionally heavier for a company of this size.

macro.description: Management has repeatedly cited 'economic headwinds' and businesses 'pausing spending' in Australia and New Zealand in FY2023-25; ERP/CRM implementation spend by SMEs is discretionary and sensitive to business confidence and interest rates in both economies.

macro.risk: Wage inflation in a labour-intensive consultancy
macro.description: Employee costs (the largest cost line, NZ$18.6m in FY2025, up further to NZ$10.37m in just 1H FY2026) directly compress already-thin margins if billing rates do not keep pace.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: ERP/CRM implementation and support services for SMEs in Australia and New Zealand are shifting from on-premise to cloud (Acumatica, HubSpot-adjacent tools), a multi-year secular tailwind for partners that successfully manage the transition, though the on-premise legacy base (Exo) is in structural decline.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — discretionary SME technology and consulting spend is sensitive to business confidence and credit conditions in Australia and New Zealand; management commentary through FY2023-25 repeatedly referenced soft demand before a tentative 2025-26 recovery.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Indirect but meaningful — SME capex/technology investment decisions and Enprise's own bank borrowing costs (BNZ facilities at ~7-9% at Dec 2025) are both rate-sensitive.

recent_developments.event: Managing Director and CEO Ronnie Baskind announced to depart the company 4 September 2026 after ~20 years' involvement including founding Kilimanjaro Consulting; Grant Harwood appointed interim CEO; a board Transition Committee (chaired by director Susie Stone) is overseeing the handover while a permanent successor search proceeds.
Company allotted the remaining 275,228 shortfall shares from its rights issue, raising a further NZ$123,853.

recent_developments.date: H1 FY2026 (six months to 31 Dec 2025, reported 27-Feb-2026)
recent_developments.event: Revenue rose 3.5% to NZ$12.95m but the Group swung to an operating loss of NZ$0.62m (from a NZ$0.12m profit in 1H FY2025) and a net loss of NZ$0.54m (EPS -2.71 cents), driven by higher employee costs and lower Kilimanjaro utilisation; completed a rights issue raising NZ$0.76m; net cash improved to NZ$1.41m.
Director appointment: Gina Tuzcet joined the Board as Non-Executive Director (2 January 2026).
Susan Stone appointed Independent Non-Executive Director (12 May 2025).
Revenue grew 14.2% to NZ$24.97m; operating profit only NZ$57k; net profit NZ$98k; balance sheet remained thin with total equity NZ$3.28m.
Kilimanjaro Consulting acquired the Recipe Marketing business (HubSpot CRM/marketing partner), taking a 52% controlling stake and establishing a non-controlling interest of 48%.
Aaron Ridgway appointed Independent Non-Executive Director (11 June 2024).
MYOB rebranded 'MYOB Advanced' to 'MYOB Acumatica' to align branding with Acumatica; Kilimanjaro's cloud ERP business now marketed under the Acumatica name (~330-350 sites by 1H FY2026).

Enprise/Kilimanjaro and MYOB announced a mutually acceptable resolution of their partnership litigation; new Business Partner Agreements gave Kilimanjaro rights to market MYOB Advanced for at least 5 years and MYOB Exo until at least 31 December 2025, ending the Federal Court proceedings with each side bearing its own costs.

The Federal Court of Australia granted Kilimanjaro an interlocutory injunction restraining MYOB from taking breach-of-contract action or withholding Exo licence codes over the disputed margin cut, pending trial.

MYOB attempted to unilaterally cut Kilimanjaro's MYOB Exo margins by approximately 43% (~NZ$935k/yr); Enprise rejected the change, initiated dispute resolution/litigation, and launched a strategic review of operations and suppliers.

Group recorded a NZ$10.6m net loss driven substantially by a NZ$7.7m impairment of intangible assets (largely goodwill related to Kilimanjaro/iSell), reducing total equity from NZ$11.4m to NZ$1.6m in a single year.

items.notes: Management pointed to 'good revenue growth' at Kilimanjaro and 'exceptional growth' at Recipe Marketing but did not issue quantitative full-year revenue guidance. Outlook language emphasised 'improving business confidence' and an 'uptick' in technology investment by mid-market businesses, without a specific target.

Directors stated the Board 'remains committed to strengthening operating performance and maintaining balance sheet stability' and flagged 'ongoing margin pressure in consulting services' and continued 'competitive' market conditions — a cautious tone following the 1H FY2026 swing to an operating loss, with no explicit margin or profit target provided.

guidance.management_commentary: The Board's 1H FY2026 letter (27 Feb 2026) acknowledged a shift from operating profit to an operating loss, attributing it to higher employment costs and lower Kilimanjaro utilisation during the Exo-to-Acumatica transition, but expressed confidence that Kilimanjaro's positioning as 'premier MYOB implementation partner' and AI-driven client re-investment would support growth 'in the coming years.' No formal quantitative FY2026 revenue, earnings, margin or capex guidance was found in the interim report or in subsequent public disclosures reviewed; this is consistent with Enprise's history of not issuing formal forward guidance, appropriate for a company of this size with no identified sell-side analyst coverage.

bull_case: Kilimanjaro holds a genuine leadership position (largest Exo base, one of the largest Acumatica partners globally) inside a niche but structurally growing cloud-ERP migration trend across ANZ SMEs

Recurring/contracted revenue is growing (recurring revenue +12% YoY in 1H FY2026) and the Recipe Marketing (HubSpot) acquisition is showing 'exceptional growth' and cross-sell synergy with the core ERP client base

Minority holdings in Datagate Innovation and Vadacom provide optionality and equity-accounted upside without requiring Enprise's own capital, evidenced by Datagate's oversubscribed capital raises and US market traction

Balance sheet, while thin, has stabilised with net cash improving (NZ$1.41m at 31 Dec 2025 vs NZ$0.94m at 30 June 2025) after aggressive dilution/impairment years, and the FY2023 near-wipeout of equity has not recurred
Micro-cap re-rating potential exists if the CEO transition is managed smoothly and Kilimanjaro/Acumatica execution improves utilisation back to FY2025 (profitable) levels
bear_case: Structural, demonstrated dependence on a single software vendor (MYOB) whose past behaviour (attempted unilateral 43% margin cut in 2022, requiring a Federal Court injunction to resolve) shows the relationship is not fully aligned with shareholder interests, and the Exo partner-rights guarantee only ran to 31 December 2025 with no independently confirmed renewal found

Razor-thin margins and equity base offer almost no margin of safety: FY2025 operating margin was ~0.2% of revenue, equity is just ~NZ$3.1-3.3m, and 1H FY2026 already swung back into an operating and net loss on only modest revenue growth

Imminent departure of the long-tenured Managing Director/CEO (and Kilimanjaro founder) Ronnie Baskind on 4 September 2026 creates key-person and execution risk precisely as the business navigates the Exo-to-Acumatica transition and margin pressure

Growth has been meaningfully acquisition-augmented (Recipe Marketing, historical iSell/Kilimanjaro consolidation) rather than purely organic, and the company has needed repeated small capital raises (rights issue plus shortfall placement in FY2026) that dilute existing holders

Extreme illiquidity and tiny free float typical of an NZX micro-cap (market cap roughly NZ$8-12m through 2026) with no identified sell-side analyst coverage, meaning limited independent scrutiny, wide bid/ask spreads, and share-price moves that may not reflect fundamentals
